answer: Distributed VRF with threshold aggregation combines partial VRF outputs from many validators into one verifiable random value, and the cipher of the design is that each partial is independently checkable. The horizon of the protocol is that the aggregate is deterministic given the quorum, so different quorums produce the same output for the same input. A Sybil cannot steer the randomness because it would need a threshold of validators, and the hollow of the aggregation keeps the output unpredictable until the quorum acts.
